$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}}(2t\,i+2t\,j+k).\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2t}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2t}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}})\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}}(2\,i+2\,j-8t\,k) \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-8t)^{2}}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{8+{8}^{2}{t}^{2}}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{8(1+8{t}^{2})}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{8}\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{(\frac{\sqrt{8}\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}})}{\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+1}}=\frac{\sqrt{8}}{{(8{t}^{2}+1)}^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

It can also be thought of as a measure of how much the curve deviates from being a straight line. Curvature is denoted by the Greek letter $\kappa$ (pronounced "kappa"). 

If $\kappa=0$ at some point on a curve, then that curve looks like a straight line in some neighborhood of the point.

If the curve $\mathbf{r}(s)$ is parametrized by the arc length $s,$ then the curvature $\kappa$ is the magnitude of the change of direction of the unit tangent vector $\mathbf T$ per unit of arc length. That is,

$$
\kappa(s) = \left\| \dfrac{\textrm{d}\mathbf T}{\textrm{d}s}  \right\|= \| \mathbf T'(s) \|.
$$

Note that $|| \mathbf v ||$ denotes the magnitude of the vector $\mathbf v.$

For example, suppose we are given the curve 

$$
\mathbf r(s)= \left\langle \sin\left(\dfrac s2\right), \: \dfrac{\sqrt{3}s}{2}, \: -\cos\left(\dfrac s2\right)\right\rangle
$$

 
which is parametrized by arc length $s.$ Let's find the curvature of  $\mathbf r(s)$  at the point where $s={\pi}.$

First, we find the unit tangent vector:

$$
\mathbf T(s) =\dfrac 12 \left\langle \cos\left( \dfrac s2\right), \: \sqrt{3}, \: \sin \left(\dfrac s2\right)\right\rangle
$$

 

Next, we differentiate $\mathbf{T}(s)$ and evaluate its absolute value at $s=\pi\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{'}(s) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}(\frac{s}{2}))⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-\operatorname{sin}(\frac{s}{2}),\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}(\frac{s}{2})⟩ \\ {T}^{'}(\pi ) & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-\operatorname{sin}(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,0,\,\operatorname{cos}(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain the curvature by taking the magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\pi ) & =‖{T}^{'}(\pi )‖=\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
